# splunkctl

> CLI tool to operate Splunk Enterprise as code — for SOC teams, detection engineers, and AI agents. Python, Click, REST API. Every mutation is dry-run by default; nothing changes until you pass --yes.

## Getting started

- [Install](https://splunkctl.danny.vn/#/guides/install): This pulls the forked SDK (splunkctl branch) automatically as a dependency.
- [Configure](https://splunkctl.danny.vn/#/guides/configure): Prompts for host, port, auth method (token or username/password), tests the connection, and writes ~/.splunkctl/config.yaml with 0600 permissions.
- [Doctor](https://splunkctl.danny.vn/#/guides/doctor): Diagnose connection, authentication, server health, and user permissions in a single command.

## Core commands

- [Search](https://splunkctl.danny.vn/#/guides/search): Run SPL queries against a remote Splunk instance from your laptop.
- [Detection rules](https://splunkctl.danny.vn/#/guides/rules): so they can live in git, pass through CI, and deploy across instances.
- [Alerts](https://splunkctl.danny.vn/#/guides/alerts): Fired alerts are the SOC's incoming work queue. During an incident, you need to see what triggered, when, and at what severity.
- [Dashboards](https://splunkctl.danny.vn/#/guides/dashboards): Uses the Dashboard/Dashboards entity classes from the SDK fork.
- [Indexes](https://splunkctl.danny.vn/#/guides/indexes): Create, configure, and manage Splunk indexes.
- [Data inputs](https://splunkctl.danny.vn/#/guides/inputs): Manage monitor, TCP, UDP, script, and HTTP data inputs.
- [Lookups](https://splunkctl.danny.vn/#/guides/lookups): Lookups turn raw events into actionable intelligence.
- [HEC tokens](https://splunkctl.danny.vn/#/guides/hec): HEC (HTTP Event Collector) is Splunk's HTTP/JSON ingestion endpoint.
- [Parsers](https://splunkctl.danny.vn/#/guides/parsers): Manage source types (props.conf) and field extractions (transforms.conf) via the REST API.
- [Apps](https://splunkctl.danny.vn/#/guides/apps): Splunk's detection and enrichment capabilities live in apps -- Technology Add-ons (TAs) for data normalization, security content packs like Splunk
- [Users and roles](https://splunkctl.danny.vn/#/guides/users): Manage Splunk users and roles via the REST API.

## Advanced

- [Macros, eventtypes, tags](https://splunkctl.danny.vn/#/guides/knowledge): Friendly, object-shaped verbs over macros.conf, eventtypes.conf, and
- [Conf](https://splunkctl.danny.vn/#/guides/conf): Generic conf file/stanza editor over the REST confs API — the escape hatch for any Splunk conf file that doesn't have a dedicated command group yet:
- [State (config-as-code, change evidence)](https://splunkctl.danny.vn/#/guides/state): snapshot of an instance's detection content, edit it like code, diff it against the live instance, then push -- with a savable before→after JSON artifact
- [ES notable-event triage](https://splunkctl.danny.vn/#/guides/es): The SOC daily loop: see what's queued, pull the full detail on one notable, then assign, set status/urgency/disposition, or leave a comment — alone or in
- [KV store (collections + data CRUD)](https://splunkctl.danny.vn/#/guides/kvstore): Splunk's KV store backs allowlists, threat-intel feeds, and Enterprise Security's asset/identity tables — schema-less JSON document storage scoped per app.
- [Change audit & RBAC attestation](https://splunkctl.danny.vn/#/guides/audit): Regulator-facing evidence for bank SOC operations: who changed what (audit changes) and who can do what (audit rbac).
- [Server Operations](https://splunkctl.danny.vn/#/guides/server): System health, license, KV store status, and topology health reads.
- [Data models (CIM/tstats acceleration)](https://splunkctl.danny.vn/#/guides/datamodels): Mature SOC detections run on accelerated CIM data models via | tstats — this group answers "which models exist," "is acceleration healthy," and "trigger a

## Design

- [Architecture](https://splunkctl.danny.vn/#/design/architecture): How splunkctl is built — the layers, the data flow, and the design decisions.
- [Catalog & status](https://splunkctl.danny.vn/#/design/catalog): The source of truth for what exists and how mature it is — one status per command group, updated in the same commit that moves it forward.
